pages.text: The next day, Julia has to go to class. "Stay in the play house," she said. "I will be back after lunch."
pages.picture: the next morning: Julia with her purple backpack on, waving goodbye on her way to class; Toby peeking out of the playhouse door
Toby alone, lying in the playhouse doorway with his chin on his paws, bored, waiting; Julia's red scooter parked on the lawn near the playhouse, both wheels fine

pages.text: After class, Julia runs to the backyard. "Toby! I am back!"
pages.picture: Julia running out of the back door and across the lawn toward the playhouse, backpack bouncing, happy, calling out

pages.text: But then she stops. Her scooter is on its side, and the wheel is bent!
pages.picture: Julia stopped short, shocked; in front of her the red scooter lies on its side on the lawn near the playhouse, its front wheel badly bent
Julia with her hands on her hips, frowning at Toby, who stands by the playhouse; the red scooter with its bent wheel lies on the grass between them

pages.text: Toby looks down at his feet. He is so, so sad. Big tears well up.
pages.picture: Toby looking down at his feet, very very sad, a big tear dripping off his nose; the red scooter with the bent wheel on the grass beside him

pages.text: Julia huffs. "That was my best scooter!" She stomps off into the house.
pages.picture: Julia stomping across the lawn toward the back door, mad, huffing, fists clenched; Toby small and sad by the playhouse behind her

pages.text: But Julia can not stay mad for long.
pages.picture: Julia standing in the open back door of the house, looking back across the lawn at the playhouse in the far corner, her mad face softening into a small smile

pages.text: Soon she is back with her kite. "Come on, Toby," she said. "Let's play."
pages.picture: Julia walking back across the lawn holding her kite, smiling; Toby peeking out of the playhouse, his face lifting
